blocks.text: In the chapter discussing the yearning that the Sahabah (RA) had for martyrdom and the du'aas they made for, in it the narration has already passed in which Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) said, "I am to make a du'aa to Allaah which I stress that every person say 'Aameen' to. (He then made the du'aa saying) O Allaah! Grant Nu'maan martyrdom today with your assistance to the Muslims and make them victorious." Another narration adds that the others then said 'Aameen' to the du'aa.[^1]
Hadhrat Dhul Bijaadayn (RA) Used to Raise his Voice when making Du'aa

Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) states, "It was with regard to a person called Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn (RA) that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Indeed, he is one who sighs very deeply.' This Rasulullaah ﷺ said because Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn (RA) used to engage in Dhikr abundantly by reciting the Qur'aan and making du'aa and all this he did in an audible voice."[^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Requests Hadhrat Umar (RA) for Du'aas and Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) requests Rasulullaah ﷺ for Du'aas

Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that when he once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ for permission to perform Umrah, Rasulullaah ﷺ granted him permission and said, "Dear brother! Do not forget us in your du'aas." Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "Those words gave me more joy than even the entire world could not."[^3]

Hadhrat Abu Umaama Baahili (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to us once, we wished that he would make du'aa for us. He then said, 'O Allaah forgive us, have mercy on us, be pleased with us, accept from us, enter us into Jannah, save us from Jahannam and mend all our affairs." When we wished that he would make more du'aa, he said, "I have already included all your affairs (in the du'aa)."[^4]
